opt2.name: The Shuttled Traverse
opt2.sub: Sisters → Oakridge, with the Wall driven

segs.name: Sisters → Camp Sherman
segs.source: Corridor approximate — likely the Metolius-Windigo Trail
segs.note: Metolius headwaters; store at Camp Sherman is the last resupply before the pass. The route file gives the waypoints but not the line, so this corridor is drawn between verified points.

segs.name: Camp Sherman → Big Lake
segs.source: Corridor approximate — via Suttle Lake and the Wagon Road
segs.note: The Wagon Road's loose volcanic pumice, laid down by Belknap Crater. Riders call the surface "frustratingly unstable" and want 2.4"+ tires. Loaded and climbing, this is the grittiest hour on either option.

segs.name: Big Lake → Clear Lake
segs.surface: Sand Mountain descent, then forest road
segs.source: Corridor approximate — waypoints verified
segs.note: Off the pass and down to Clear Lake.

segs.name: Clear Lake → Trail Bridge — the lava
segs.source: Measured — OSM way geometry, USGS NED 10 m at 0.1 mi
segs.note: The hard part of the MRT and the only Advanced-rated riding on either option. Sahalie and Koosah falls, then Blue Pool. Riders call it fatiguing and occasionally unrideable — in either direction. Almost none of the difficulty is gradient; it is all rock.

segs.name: Trail Bridge → McKenzie Bridge — the flow
segs.source: Measured — OSM way geometry, USGS NED 10 m at 0.1 mi
segs.note: What the MRT is famous for: twelve miles of fast, buffed singletrack beside the river. Bigelow and Belknap hot springs are both on it.

segs.name: McKenzie Bridge → FR-19 junction
segs.source: Measured — OSM way geometry
segs.note: Paved. The original plan calls this leg King Castle / Olallie / O'Leary singletrack, but its own GPX puts McKenzie Bridge to Cougar at 12.4 mi with 365 ft of gain — a road profile, not a ridge one. Those trails top out above 5,000 ft.

segs.name: FR-19 junction → Cougar Hot Springs
segs.source: Measured — USGS NED 10 m
segs.note: Still paved, still gentle. Soak at Terwilliger, then meet the van.

segs.name: THE WALL — driven, not ridden
segs.source: Measured — USGS NED 10 m
segs.note: 11.7 miles and 3,137 ft, the last 7.5 of it at a sustained 7.2%. The climb the van exists to delete. Option 3 rides it; Option 5 never goes near it.

segs.name: Indian Ridge → Elk Camp
segs.source: GROUP GPX ONLY — corridor not verified
segs.note: The miles that make Option 2 long. Technically moderate, but 23.7 miles with no water, no bail-out and no cell service. This is the one stretch I could not match to OSM geometry — endpoints right, line approximate.

segs.name: Elk Camp → Sourgrass
segs.source: Corridor approximate
segs.note: Short climb out of the dry camp to the top of the Alpine.

segs.name: Alpine Trail → Westfir
segs.source: Measured — OSM way geometry, USGS NED 10 m at 0.2 mi
segs.note: The payoff, identical to Option 5's Day 3. Note the route file gives this day as 14.2 mi; the Alpine alone measures 16.2.

segs.name: Westfir → Oakridge
segs.source: Corridor approximate
segs.note: Past the covered bridge into town.

opt5.name: The Oakridge Trail Finish
opt5.sub: Sisters → Oakridge, with the byway driven

segs.source: Corridor approximate — waypoints verified

segs.name: Transfer — the Aufderheide by van
segs.source: Measured — OSM way geometry
segs.note: About 75 minutes to Alpine Trailhead #5 at 3,779 ft. The whole connector problem, solved by declining to ride it. Option 4 spends two days on this road; Option 2 rides 23.7 miles of ridge above it.

segs.name: Alpine Trail
segs.source: Measured — OSM way geometry, USGS NED 10 m at 0.2 mi
segs.note: 16.2 miles, +1,702 / −4,327. The ride that put Oakridge on the map, rated 4.5/5 on MTB Project. Forgiving enough for a strong intermediate on an unloaded bike.

segs.name: Westfir → Oakridge
segs.source: Corridor approximate
segs.note: Into town for the night.

segs.name: Larison Rock Road climb
segs.source: Corridor approximate — paved shuttle road
segs.note: Option 5's only real pavement, and a climb you could shuttle instead. 6.8 miles to 3,301 ft.

segs.name: Larison Rock descent
segs.source: Measured — OSM way geometry, USGS NED 10 m at 0.15 mi
segs.note: 3.0 miles, −2,014 ft, continuous. Trailforks rates it black diamond, MTB Project difficult. The hardest descending on either option.
